Authorize each individual customer account through OAuth

prohibitions: Uploading, editing, moving, or deleting files or folders
guide.summary: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 user tokens for per-account access. The list-folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read and its continue endpoint uses the same scope. The app must be created with App Folder access so reads stay within the app folder. Registration and redirect URIs are setup prerequisites. Distribution to other customer organizations is not covered by the supplied snapshots.
guide.recommendation: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 user tokens for per-account access. The list-folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read and its continue endpoint uses the same scope. The app must be created with App Folder access so reads stay within the app folder. Registration and redirect URIs are setup prerequisites. Distribution to other customer organizations is not covered by the supplied snapshots.

findings.title: Per-account user OAuth 2.0 code flow is documented
findings.detail: Dropbox documents the OAuth 2.0 code flow as the recommended flow for all application types. Apps that request only User API scopes receive a token tied to the user who authorizes the app, which fits individual customer accounts. Tokens are short-lived and sent as a Bearer header.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer authorizes its own Dropbox account and no team administration is used.

evidence.quote: is the recommended OAuth flow for all types of applications. In order to implement it, your application should:
Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user
Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.

findings.title: files.metadata.read: view information about files and folders
findings.detail: The scope description covers viewing information about files and folders. The list_folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read for user tokens, and list_folder/continue requires the same scope. The scope does not permit downloading or changing content.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing file and folder names with list_folder and list_folder/continue.

evidence.quote: Scope Description files.metadata.read View information about files and folders
Required scope: files.metadata.read Endpoint format: RPC
list_folder . Required scope: files.metadata.read

findings.title: Create the app with App Folder access type
findings.detail: The app must be created as a scoped app with App folder access, which limits actions to data within the app folder. This is an app setting, not an OAuth grant. Full Dropbox access is not needed for the requested listing.
findings.appliesWhen: Always, to restrict listing to the app folder.

evidence.quote: App folder : Access limited to a single folder in the user’s Dropbox.

findings.title: Register the app key, secret and exact redirect URIs before OAuth testing
findings.detail: Before OAuth can start, register the app in the Developer Console to obtain the app key and secret and register each exact redirect URI under the OAuth 2 section. Dropbox checks that the redirect_uri in the authorization URL matches a registered value.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first OAuth authorization test.
